design_assessment.canonical_fields_preserved: Branch, active state, base SHA, and exact allowed-path set remain sourced from and checked against the canonical task row; the pin does not override them. Work ID is explicitly VIS-04.
design_assessment.coverage: Positive q38/q34 fixture plus old tuple and isolated wrong-owner, wrong-token, and wrong-accepted-revision negative cases cover the requested migration. Negative cases retain blocked receipts and assert no Nextest list/run and zero executions.
design_assessment.explicit_caller_pin: The required --claim-pin path supplies an out-of-band expected work ID, owner, token, and accepted revision; helper compares these against the canonical single VIS-04 row and does not derive them from tasks.json.
design_assessment.revision_semantics: Accepted revision 34 is compared to the caller pin and canonical task record; top-level current revision 38 is separately read, checked as integer >= accepted revision, and preserved independently in receipt.
design_assessment.scope: Two source files are sufficient for a CLI argument/validator change and its Rust black-box integration controls. The design excludes product code and leaves the existing S1d result untouched.

findings.finding: The README promises a mismatched pin is rejected before tool setup, but proposed negative assertions name no Nextest list/run invocation only. Assert the fixture trace contains no tool setup/version probe as well (or narrow the wording). Current call order validates the claim before environment/tool setup, so this is a test precision note, not a design blocker.

limitations: The pin is a caller-supplied consistency expectation, not a signature or authentication credential. Its independence depends on the invoking workflow supplying a separately fixed value; the helper must never synthesize it from tasks.json.
This review approves the design for bounded implementation only. The implementation and new Rust controls remain unreviewed and unrun.
No product assertions were rerun. The existing S1d 23-test result remains a separate product lane; this proposal changes only the deferred harness and its Rust controls.
observations: The frozen proposal, README, and packet manifest hashes match the review request; all three manifest file hashes and byte counts verified.
The proposal-bound production/helper and Rust test source hashes match the current source files.

At review time, the canonical task registry is q38 and has one VIS-04 row owned by /root with token visibility-deferred-root-q33-20261009-01 and accepted revision 34. Branch, claimed state, accepted base, and all four allowed paths match the proposal.

The current production helper still pins the obsolete owner /root/current_branch_comparison_luna, token visibility-deferred-recovery-20261008-04, and accepted revision 24. Its validator currently requires exactly one VIS-04 row, checks owner/token, termrock-implementation and claimed/in_progress state, accepted revision, exact allowed-path set, then records top-level queue_revision separately. It validates the claim before environment capture, Nextest version/list/run calls.
The current Rust fixture uses q24 for both current and accepted revision; the existing positive receipt test asserts both as 24, so it must be updated to q38/q34.
scope: Read-only design review of the frozen VIS-04 explicit claim-pin proposal. No source edits, tests, Cargo, Nextest, or product run.
